title: OSHA Rebar Cap Checklist (29 CFR 1926.701)
subtitle: For site walks during concrete work: rebar guards, loads, the tensioning area, buckets and pneumatic application.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
For any Defect, stop the exposed work or keep employees away until it is corrected, then record the fix.
Manufacturer's instructions and site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: Protruding reinforcing steel
items: Every protruding bar end below or beside a work area or walkway is guarded.
Protruding bars in openings, forms or excavations are guarded.
Guards are in place, undamaged and cover the bar so a falling worker could not be impaled.

sections.title: Construction loads
items: Information from a person qualified in structural design is available for the structure or portion being loaded.
The employer has determined, from that information, that the structure or portion can support the planned loads.
No construction loads sit on any concrete structure or portion that has not been assessed.

sections.title: Post-tensioning operations
items: During tensioning, only employees essential to the post-tensioning work are behind the jack.
Signs are erected to limit employee access to the post-tensioning area while tensioning is under way.
Barriers are erected around the post-tensioning area while tensioning is under way.

sections.title: Concrete buckets and pneumatic hose application
items: No employee rides a concrete bucket.
No employee is under a concrete bucket while it is being elevated or lowered into position.
Elevated buckets follow a route that exposes no employees, or the fewest practical, to a falling bucket.
Each employee applying cement, sand and water mixture through a pneumatic hose wears protective head equipment.
Each employee applying the mixture through a pneumatic hose wears protective face equipment.

references: 29 CFR 1926.701: General requirements (Part 1926 Subpart Q, Concrete and Masonry Construction)
